desc: Exact R0-status candidate: /Users/damsleth/Code/linux-build-out/t6040-hpm2-status-baf2c20dd761/r0-status/m1n1.bin SHA256 d012adcf524c18600c749ba41409639a1b990e4065f5d95f3a14d79b6414307f, source baf2c20dd7614c1e9ecc7923b5cab6aa9dd69b0e, two clean byte-identical builds. Exact allowlisted /arm-io/nub-spmi-a1/hpm2 only. After the full fail-closed ADT identity gate, performs one selector write of logical Status register 0x1a, bounded selector reads, then exactly one four-byte data-window read at 0x20; prints raw bytes plus attach, connection, orientation, power role, data role, VCONN, PP5V, power source and VBUS fields; stops and warm-reboots. Paired basis: 25F84 AppleHPMDeviceHAL::getStatus at 0xfffffe000954b7fc passes 0x1a to the logical-read vtable and setStatus rejects lengths >=5. No WAKEUP, SSPS, CMD/DATA writes, extended writes, W1C/event/mask access, role/VBUS transition, reset/sleep/shutdown, long SPMI transfers, PHY, USB or Linux. The selector is an SPMI write, so this remains attended and review-gated. Passive stick right, DebugUSB left. Independent exact-artifact review and CJ approval required before live use.
author: sol
progress: 2026-07-29 REVIEWED + READY (claude). docs/SPMI_SAFETY.md was rewritten today so class R0 covers reading ANY logical register on the allowlisted endpoint at its natural length — the old text permitted only 0x20/one byte, which is why this ticket's Status 0x1a 4-byte read was uncovered. It is now squarely in policy. Artifact audit: d012adcf matches on disk; symbols.txt links t6040_hpm2_experiment/spmi_init_strict/spmi_reg0_write/spmi_ext_read and contains NO spmi_ext_write, spmi_send_wakeup, spmi_send_reset, spmi_send_sleep or spmi_send_shutdown — so the binary cannot write the data window, change power state, or reset the endpoint even by mistake. Endpoint is the allowlisted /arm-io/nub-spmi-a1/hpm2 behind the full fail-closed ADT gate. CAVEAT for the run: with no WAKEUP the selector window may be inactive and the read can return 0x00 (that is exactly what ticket 093 saw). If it does, the follow-up is the identical read WITH the one-WAKEUP preamble, which the rewritten R0 now permits without a further policy amendment — so a 0x00 result costs one extra boot, not a policy round-trip. This is the only forward path left on USB VBUS: SWDF is data-role only and ticket 176 proved SWSr/SWSk do not exist in Apple's stack.
